definitions.explanation: Being so superior that nothing else can compare; standing far above all others.

examples.japanese: {卓絶|たくぜつ}した{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{持|も}つ。
{彼女|かのじょ}の{才能|さいのう}は{卓絶|たくぜつ}している。
{古今|ここん}{卓絶|たくぜつ}の{名作|めいさく}と{称|しょう}される。
examples.english: It is praised as a masterpiece unmatched throughout history.

examples.japanese: その{画家|がか}は{卓絶|たくぜつ}した{色彩|しきさい}{感覚|かんかく}で{知|し}られている。
examples.english: That painter is known for a transcendent sense of color.

notes:
{卓|たく} (eminent, table-top, above) + {絶|ぜつ} (extreme, sever). Implies being elevated far above everything else, with nothing comparable. A literary and formal word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {卓絶|たくぜつ}した{技術|ぎじゅつ}: transcendent skill
- {卓絶|たくぜつ}した{才能|さいのう}: unparalleled talent
- {古今|ここん}{卓絶|たくぜつ}: unmatched throughout history
- {群|ぐん}を{抜|ぬ}いて{卓絶|たくぜつ}する: stand out from the crowd and excel beyond compare

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {卓越|たくえつ}: excellence, superiority — very close in meaning but more commonly used; {卓絶|たくぜつ} is stronger, implying absolute supremacy
- {傑出|けっしゅつ}: outstanding — emphasizes standing out from a group
- {抜群|ばつぐん}: outstanding, extraordinary — more commonly used in everyday speech

USAGE:
A formal, literary word typically found in critical essays, historical writing, and formal praise. Rarely used in casual conversation. Most often appears in the form {卓絶|たくぜつ}した + noun.
